paper.title_en: Model-independent Constraints on Dark Energy Density from CMB-SPA, DESI DR2 BAO, and Updated Type Ia Supernova Compilations
paper.abstract_en: Recent combinations of DESI BAO, CMB, and Type~Ia supernova data report a preference for evolving dark energy that is obtained within the $(w_0, w_a)$ parameterization and depends on the choice of SN~Ia compilation. We constrain the dark energy density ratio $X(z) \equiv ρ_{\rm DE}(z)/ρ_{\rm DE}(0)$ at five redshifts over $0 < z < 2.33$, without assuming a parametric form for the equation of state, using CMB data from SPT-3G, Planck~2018, and ACT~DR6 (hereafter CMB-SPA), DESI~DR2 BAO, and the updated Pantheon+, Union3.1, and DES-Dovekie SN~Ia compilations. For all three compilations, $X(z)$ rises above unity at low redshift, crosses unity near $z \approx 1$, and falls below unity at higher redshift. Depending on the SN~Ia compilation, the preference for a departure from a cosmological constant is $2.3$--$2.8σ$ with the five $X(z)$ knots, compared with $3.0$--$3.2σ$ in the $(w_0, w_a)$ parameterization. Because $X(z)$ is constrained locally in redshift, we can trace how the $Λ$CDM tension between each pair of probes propagates into its shape. The tension between BAO and the CMB in the $h r_d$--$Ω_m$ plane reproduces this "see-saw" shape, whereas the $Ω_m$ tension between SNe~Ia and the CMB only raises $X(z)$ slightly and nearly uniformly. The origin of the BAO--CMB tension can be tested by Euclid and Roman BAO measurements at $z \gtrsim 1$. We derive the distance prior $(R, \ell_A, ω_b)$ from CMB-SPA data and show that it retains essentially all the information on $X(z)$ in the CMB-SPA power spectra without the lensing reconstruction, and that adding the lensing reconstruction only marginally increases the information on dark energy. Our work demonstrates the importance of model independence in exploring the nature of dark energy.
